guide.title: Bounded elimination and generator selection
guide.summary: certified relations decide a small generator set by elimination (one lex order, or a bounded search by size whose undecided sets are recorded, never guessed), every eliminated column's polynomial reconstruction certified by FND-007 and checked on every row (values, NULL domains, ranges), local elimination forms of a query costed on actual bit widths and scans with the direct form kept whenever expansion loses; checks on the CPU and in CUDA.

GEOM-002.cpu: Native generator selection, reconstructions, local elimination forms, row checks and costs over an FND-004 scope and GEOM-001 relations (up to 16 FND-007 certificates over at most 8 variables). A generator set G has a reconstruction x = f_x(G) for every eliminated variable exactly when, under lex with the eliminated variables first, GEOM-001's reduced Groebner basis reduces x into Q[G] (the elimination property); f_x is that normal form and its FND-007 derived certificate D (x - f_x) = sum D h_k r_k is GEOM-001's reduction certificate. Two modes: one elimination under a given lex sequence (one solve), or a bounded search by increasing size over every subset of the relation variables in lexicographic order (variables in no relation always generators), one completion per set, ranked by a declared priority (total, scan, work, bits; ties to the earliest) among the sets of the minimum size; a set whose completion passes the degree or support budget, GEOM-001's per-solve limit or int64 is recorded as undecided (with its refusal) and the search goes on, minimality claimed only when every smaller set was decided. A reconstruction is kept only when its row check holds: on every selected row the target column and the reconstruction are evaluated exactly in W <= 8 64-bit words under a bound proven from the scope's extremes (DISC-002's evaluation), with SQL NULL propagation (null_lost / null_extra NULL-domain mismatches), value mismatches, the target column's range (below, above, both ends attained) and the smallest mismatching row of each kind. Costs are measured on the scope: widths from max - min of the present values plus a validity plane, scan = ceil(N / 64) x widths read, work = N x (terms + multiplications) x words from the actual bit length of every evaluated row, a generator set's storage plus its reconstructions, each column's read path (reconstruct only when strictly cheaper than its stored scan). Local elimination forms of a query q: q as written, every substitution of a nonempty set of the eliminated variables q reads (GEOM-001 division by their reconstruction certificates, certified by FND-007 at depth 2) and optionally the normal form under the selection's elimination ideal; each checked against q on every row and costed on its own integer form, the cheapest admissible chosen and ties kept by the direct form, so a term explosion or cost regression keeps q. Budgets: iterations = solves (refused at the limit + 1), degree and support bound every completion and reduction (an order selection refused, a form rejected with its refusal), variables, output and bytes checked before allocation.
GEOM-002.gpu: tr_mgpu_elim_check: work items (a chunk of 8 pairs, a row slice of at least 64 selection words) run the inline tr_elim_pair_row shared with the CPU on each selected row of their slice for every pair of their chunk: the target's and the form's NULL domains, their exact W-word integer forms under the bound the host proved, the form against the target column's range; they count locally and add one atomic per nonzero counter, the smallest mismatching rows by atomic minimum and the largest bit lengths by atomic maximum, so the results (and the first mismatching row) do not depend on the order threads run in and equal tr_elim_check_view bit for bit. The host validates the pair view (its structure and the view's extremes within the magnitudes the bounds were proven for) and budgets the device copies before launching. Selection, completion, reduction and certification run on the CPU. Compiled with nvcc for sm_80 and tested in the emulation with scrambled thread order; not yet run on a device.
limitations: Reconstructions are polynomials in the generators (no rational, algebraic or implicit reconstructions); a column that is only algebraic over the others stays a generator.

The search is exponential in the number of variables (at most 255 sets for 8) and its lex completions grow quickly: with dense or implicitization-like sets many are undecided under the budget or int64, and minimality is then not claimed.
Coefficients are GEOM-001's int64 rationals (no arbitrary precision); a reconstruction or form past int64 is undecided or unclaimable, never rounded.
A reconstruction is exact where its relations hold: a snapshot relation makes it exact on that snapshot's rows only (FND-007 staleness applies).
Costs are relative work units of the bit-plane engine measured on one scope (widths, scans, word counts), not a planner's timing model.
The CUDA kernel covers the batched row checks; selection, completion, reduction and certification run on the CPU.
The CUDA kernel has been compiled with nvcc and verified in the emulation only; no device run yet.
